name: SPARKLINE
description: SPARKLINE creates a miniature chart inside a single cell, perfect for visualizing trends in a row or column of data without taking up much space.
tldr: SPARKLINE draws a tiny chart in a cell from a range of numbers, with options for line, bar, column, and win/loss charts.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The range or array of numeric values to chart. Must be one-dimensional (a single row or column).

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: An optional string or array of options to customize the chart, such as charttype, color, linewidth, max, min, etc.

basicExample.description: Create a simple line sparkline for monthly sales
basicExample.explanation: A2:A13 contains monthly sales numbers. SPARKLINE draws a small line chart in the cell.

advancedExamples.title: Column sparkline with color
advancedExamples.description: Show daily values as colored columns
advancedExamples.explanation: The options specify a column chart with blue bars. Options are passed as an array of key-value pairs.

advancedExamples.title: Win/loss sparkline
advancedExamples.description: Show positive values as blue wins and negative values as red losses
advancedExamples.explanation: Win/loss charts show only whether each value is positive or negative, not the magnitude.

howItWorks: SPARKLINE takes a one-dimensional range of numbers and renders a small chart in the cell. The chart type and appearance are controlled by an options array. Supported types include line, bar, column, and win/loss. The chart resizes automatically with the cell.

howToSteps.name: Select the data range
howToSteps.text: Choose a single row or column of numbers.

howToSteps.name: Choose a chart type
howToSteps.text: Default is line. Use 'column', 'bar', or 'winloss' for other styles.

howToSteps.name: Add options
howToSteps.text: Pass options as {'option', value; ...} to customize color, min, max, etc.

limitations: SPARKLINE is Google Sheets only. Excel has its own Sparkline feature via Insert > Sparkline, but not as a worksheet function.
Only one-dimensional data works; a 2D range will cause an error.
Advanced chart customization is limited compared to full charts.
Text and empty cells in the data range may cause errors or gaps.

commonErrors.cause: The data range is two-dimensional or contains non-numeric values.
commonErrors.fix: Use a single row or column and ensure all values are numbers.

commonErrors.cause: The cell is too small or the formula returned an error.
commonErrors.fix: Widen the cell and check the formula for errors.
Use the array syntax {'key', value; 'key2', value2} with semicolons separating rows.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: SPARKLINE is native to Google Sheets. Excel offers Sparkline charts via the Insert menu, not as a function.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Excel's Sparkline feature is a chart object, while Google Sheets uses a formula-based approach.

faq.question: Can SPARKLINE show multiple series?
faq.answer: No, it only supports one-dimensional data. For multiple series, use a full chart.

faq.question: Can I use SPARKLINE in Excel?
faq.answer: Excel has Sparkline charts via Insert > Sparkline, but not a SPARKLINE worksheet function.

faq.question: How do I change the line color?
Can I highlight the maximum value?
faq.answer: Yes, use the highcolor option or combine with max in a custom formula for conditional coloring.
